summary.en: ChrysCapital, founded in 1999 by Ashish Dhawan, is one of India's longest-tenured and largest homegrown growth-equity / private equity firms. In November 2025 it closed Fund X at $2.2 billion, the largest India-focused PE fund ever raised. It has invested ~$4.5 billion across 100+ investments and raised $5 billion across nine prior funds.

It is sector-agnostic and makes long-term growth investments, MBOs and spin-offs in mid-sized Indian companies.

summary.en: Kedaara Capital is a Mumbai-based India-focused growth-equity and buyout firm. In 2024 it raised a record $1.74 billion Fund IV — at the time India's largest PE fund — exceeding its $1.5 billion target and 54% larger than its $1.08 billion Fund III (2021). It pursues control and minority investments across financial services, consumer, technology and pharma/healthcare.

summary.en: Norwest Venture Partners is a US-headquartered (Menlo Park) multi-stage fund with a dedicated India practice based in Mumbai since 2009, led by Niren Shah. It makes growth-equity investments of $20M–$100M in India-centric businesses (and $10M–$30M at early/mid stage). Norwest closed its 17th global fund (NVP 17) at $3 billion in 2024 and has backed 43 Indian companies including Swiggy, OfBusiness, Mensa Brands and Amagi.
